ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows that diagonal BD is drawn in quadrilateral ABCD, and BD divides the quadrilateral into two triangles: triangle ABD and triangle BCD. Let BD=x. From the side lengths given in the problem, the three sides of triangle ABD are AB=5, AD=9, and BD=x, so the triangle inequality gives |9-5|<x<9+5, namely 4<x<14. The three sides of triangle BCD are BC=17, CD=5, and BD=x, so |17-5|<x<17+5, namely 12<x<22. Combining the two ranges gives 12<x<14. Because the problem states that BD is an integer, the only possible integer is x=13.

method.method_draft: Let x=BD. From the image, diagonal BD divides the quadrilateral into triangles ABD and BCD. From the text, triangle ABD has side lengths 5, 9, and x, so the triangle inequality gives |9-5|<x<9+5, hence 4<x<14. Triangle BCD has side lengths 17, 5, and x, so |17-5|<x<17+5, hence 12<x<22. Combining gives 12<x<14. Since the text says BD is an integer, x=13.

method.method_draft: Let x=BD. Use an algebraic feasibility approach via the Law of Cosines. In triangle ABD, the sides adjacent to the included angle at A are AB=5 and AD=9, so x^2=5^2+9^2-2(5)(9)cos A. Since the triangle is nondegenerate, -1<cos A<1, which implies (9-5)^2<x^2<(9+5)^2, so 4<x<14. In triangle BCD, x^2=17^2+5^2-2(17)(5)cos C, and -1<cos C<1 gives (17-5)^2<x^2<(17+5)^2, so 12<x<22. Therefore 12<x<14, and the only integer value is x=13.
